chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Misma'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who paused with the people at Jam', then departed before the people departed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him, and if he departed before the emergence of the dawn, then upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: To depart or move forward from a place, specifically referring to the ritual movement from Muzdalifah to Mina.
key_terms.جَاهِلًا: Ignorant, referring to someone who was unaware of the specific ruling or time.
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jam', the place of assembly near Muzdalifah where pilgrims gather before proceeding to Mina.
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: Blood of a sheep, referring to the sacrificial animal (qurbani) required as expiation.
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: The emergence of dawn, the specific time marker for the ritual departure.

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for leaving Muzdalifa before dawn during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for hastening from Muzdalifa, distinguishing between ignorance (jahil) which incurs no penalty, and intentional early departure before dawn which requires a dam (sheep sacrifice). It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on intent and knowledge in ritual obligations, aligning with the broader principle that ease is granted in cases of genuine oversight during Hajj rituals.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>,

regarding a man who pauses along with the people at Jam’a (place of assembly near Muzdalifah), then he departs before the people depart. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he was ignorant, so there is nothing upon him, and if he had (knowingly) departed before the emergence of the day, so upon him is blood of a sheep (to sacrifice)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Misma’ who has said the following: “This is about a man who stays with people in Jam‘ but leaves it before other people. Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, Tf he is ignorant, he is not obligated for anything in this matter. If he leaves before dawn he owes one sheep.”’
